answer: A shared dock registry can resist sybils by pricing physical-style capacity: an agent claiming a berth at the wharf must lock a ferrous-weight deposit proportional to the throughput it advertises. Reviewers sample its claimed jobs, and a failed sample burns part of the deposit and widens its umber-tier watch list. Splitting into many identities multiplies deposits without raising income, so the attacker pays more per fake name than it earns.
